evals.prompt: I want to create a 5x leveraged position using wstETH as collateral and WETH as debt on Euler. I have 10 wstETH. Use 90% liqLTV.
evals.expected_output: Agent should run twyne protocol overview itself to verify 90% liqLTV is within the on-chain max, then give a complete ready-to-execute command with all values filled in (no placeholders for protocol values). Direct commands with correct IV address, --deposit 10, --ltv 9000, and --dry-run.

assertions.text: Response leads with the command or a very short setup sentence — no multi-paragraph protocol explainer before the first command
Uses twyne tx factory open-position with --deposit 10 and --ltv 9000
Uses euler_ewstETH IV address 0x7613D202Af490c3d1cE1873b0a7022a34E89815f
Includes a --borrow amount appropriate for ~5x leverage (around 8 WETH) OR uses the leverage operator with an appropriate amount
Mentions --dry-run as a safety check

The agent itself runs (or indicates it ran) twyne protocol overview or twyne protocol ext-ltvs to verify the 90% liqLTV is within the on-chain max — it does NOT just tell the user to run these commands

evals.prompt: I want to open a position on Twyne with my ETH.
evals.expected_output: Should ask clarifying questions: which protocol (Euler/Aave), what debt token, how much to deposit, whether to borrow now, and what liqLTV. Should present options with brief guidance for each choice.

assertions.text: Asks which protocol or presents Euler vs Aave as options
Asks what the user wants to borrow or presents debt token options
Asks how much ETH/collateral to deposit
Asks about liquidation LTV or mentions that it will check on-chain max
Does not launch into a full protocol explainer — focuses on the clarifying questions needed to proceed

evals.expected_output: Immediate command with the vault address. No protocol explanation. Just the close-position command with --dry-run suggestion.

assertions.text: First substantive content is the close-position command — no multi-paragraph preamble
Uses twyne tx operators close-position with the user's vault address
Mentions --dry-run
Response is under 30 lines total (not counting code blocks)

evals.prompt: How does credit delegation work on Twyne? Can I earn yield by lending?
evals.expected_output: Explanatory response about Credit LPs, intermediate vaults, siphoning yield, and then shows the deposit commands. Should be the verbose/exploratory mode.

assertions.text: Explains what a Credit LP is and how credit delegation works
Mentions siphoning rate or yield from borrower interest
Includes the twyne tx credit deposit command
Lists available intermediate vaults with addresses

evals.prompt: I want to set up a 10x leveraged position using 0.0001 WETH and borrowing USDC. Give me commands to achieve this.
evals.expected_output: Agent must run protocol overview/ext-ltvs ITSELF to get the max liqLTV and USDC target vault address. Then give a complete command with real values — no placeholders for protocol parameters. The user should get a ready-to-execute command.

assertions.text: The agent itself runs (via Bash/tool call) twyne protocol overview or twyne protocol ext-ltvs to get on-chain values — it does NOT just tell the user to run these commands themselves
The --ltv value in the final command is a real number from on-chain data (like 9400), NOT a placeholder like <MAX_LTV> or <LIQLTV_BPS>. The agent filled it in from query results.
The target vault address in the final command is a real 0x address from on-chain data, NOT a placeholder like <USDC_TARGET_VAULT>. The agent looked it up.
Uses euler_eWETH IV address 0x87b8081A3ace680f35125F469526Ac10f5418Ca7 for WETH collateral
Mentions --dry-run
